headline: A 2018 Senate budget resolution for fiscal year 2019 that was not taken up or debated, so it never became binding.
what_it_does: If adopted, this concurrent resolution would have set spending, revenue, and deficit targets for the federal government for fiscal year 2019 and projected levels through 2028. It would have instructed several Senate committees to write bills cutting the deficit, and told the Senate Finance Committee to write both deficit-reduction and revenue-reduction bills. It would also have created reserve funds giving the Senate some room to apply budget rules to savings from efficiency and consolidation measures and to health savings accounts.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies and programs funded by annual appropriations
who_it_affects.how: They would have operated under the spending limits set by this budget plan for fiscal years 2019 through 2028.

who_it_affects.group: Members of Congress and Senate committees
who_it_affects.how: Several Senate committees would have been directed to write deficit-reduction bills, and the Finance Committee would have been directed to write deficit-reduction and revenue-reduction bills under expedited procedures.

who_it_affects.group: People who save in health savings accounts
who_it_affects.how: Reserve funds would have allowed the Senate more flexibility to consider legislation relating to these accounts without the usual budget limits applying.

who_it_affects.group: Social Security beneficiaries and Postal Service customers
who_it_affects.how: The plan would have set specific budget levels for Social Security and Postal Service administrative expenses in the Senate.
